items.headline: Governor Shapiro signs executive order demanding strict requirements for data centers
items.summary: Governor Josh Shapiro signed Executive Order 2026-05 directing Pennsylvania agencies to require data-center developers to meet the Governor's Responsible Infrastructure Development requirements and obtain local approval. The order removes AI data-center proposals from the state's fast-track permitting program and bars nondisclosure agreements for data-center projects.

items.headline: Florida regulators approve JEA's need for a 675-megawatt combined-cycle plant
items.summary: The Florida Public Service Commission approved JEA's need for additional power to support construction of the SJRPP 3 combined-cycle plant. JEA said the $1.57 billion project remains on schedule to come online in 2031 and will support Northeast Florida's growing energy demand.

items.headline: Bexar County proposes $2.6 billion budget while holding tax rate steady
items.summary: Bexar County commissioners reviewed a proposed 2026-27 budget of $2.6 billion that reduces a projected future shortfall from $145 million to $42 million. The proposal holds the property-tax rate below 30 cents per $100, approves no net new general-fund hires, and sets a final budget vote for September 15.

items.headline: North Carolina governor vetoes election overhaul bill
items.summary: Governor Josh Stein vetoed House Bill 958, which would have required voter-roll cross-checks with death records, reduced early-voting days in some elections, and expanded the state auditor's election-review powers. The Daily Signal reported that Republican lawmakers had enough votes to attempt an override.

items.headline: Peraton wins approximately $117 million Army cybersecurity recompete
items.summary: Peraton was awarded a mission-critical program to continue cybersecurity and network operations for the U.S. Army Regional Cyber Center–Europe. The recompete contract is valued at approximately $117 million and runs through 2031.

items.headline: NCDHHS and UNC partner to expand suicide-prevention training
items.summary: The North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services is partnering with the UNC School of Social Work to expand Mental Health First Aid training to UNC-system universities and community-college campuses during 2026-27. The project plans at least 50 sessions, reaching at least 15 institutions and training 600 participants, and will also offer training to NCDHHS employees.
items.entityName: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services
items.source: North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services

items.headline: Thousands of JEA customers lose power after Northeast Florida storms
items.summary: Storms across Clay, Duval and St. Johns counties caused weather-related outages for JEA customers. At one point 8,038 customers, about 1.47% of JEA's 546,281 served customers, were without power; 4,065 remained without power as of 6 p.m.

items.headline: CMS renews PCG's Quality Improvement Organization-Like designation through 2031
items.summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services renewed Public Consulting Group's Quality Improvement Organization-Like Entity designation through 2031. PCG said the designation supports its Medicaid quality-assurance, utilization-review, oversight and improvement work, including work with state Medicaid agencies.

items.headline: Florida CFO highlights 45 fraud arrests in July
items.summary: Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia highlighted 45 arrests in July arising from investigations by the Department of Financial Services' fraud and fire-investigation bureaus. The department said the arrests included insurance fraud, public-assistance fraud, and fire, arson and explosives investigations.

items.headline: New York health department backs science-based vaccination recommendations
items.summary: The New York State Department of Health issued a statement on behalf of the Northeast Public Health Collaborative supporting science-based vaccination recommendations. The statement said undermining confidence in the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine could lead to additional cases and deaths during a major measles outbreak.
items.entityName: New York State Department of Health
items.source: New York State Department of Health

items.headline: Phoenix nears 200-mile Cool Pavement milestone
items.summary: The City of Phoenix expected to surpass 200 miles of Cool Pavement installed on city streets by the end of the week. The asphalt-based treatment is part of the city's heat-mitigation and routine street-maintenance programs.

items.headline: Maricopa County reports heat deaths more than double last year's level at the same point
items.summary: Maricopa County had confirmed 81 heat-related deaths in 2026 as of August 18, compared with 35 at the same point in 2025. Another 587 deaths remained under investigation as potentially heat-related, up from 376 at the same point last year.

items.headline: Ingoglia and Taddeo win party nominations for Florida CFO
items.summary: Blaise Ingoglia won the Republican primary for Florida chief financial officer and Annette Taddeo won the Democratic nomination. The two candidates are scheduled to face each other in the November 3 general election for an office that oversees the Florida Department of Financial Services.

items.headline: NYITCOM at A-State and UA Little Rock launch seven-year medical-school pathway
items.summary: The New York Institute of Technology College of Osteopathic Medicine at Arkansas State University and UA Little Rock established a pathway allowing qualified students to earn undergraduate and medical degrees in seven years. The program will admit up to 10 students annually and expects its first cohort in spring 2027.

items.headline: Ohio University warns food-truck vendors about impersonation scam
items.summary: Ohio Athletics warned that fraudulent emails are impersonating its director of marketing and soliciting food-truck vendors for Peden Stadium. The university said it is not seeking vendors for that venue, does not charge vendors to participate, and advised recipients to verify Ohio.edu senders and report suspicious messages.
